messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a provisioning queue spike in us-west-2 for GPU nodepools, several pods Pending >6m. Cluster-autoscaler shows scale attempt but nodes stuck in 'Provisioning'.
aj: Can you paste the kubectl -> events / describe from one of the pending pods?
sanjay: found this on the nodegroup: 'InstanceLaunchRateExceeded' and a bunch of ENI attach failures in the same time window.
maria: paste: ```Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  7m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned inference/worker-42 to <none>
  Warning FailedCreatePod 6m kubelet            failed to create pod: timed out waiting for the condition
```
aj: AWS side looks like ENI attach throttling + API rate limit from our autoscaler requests. us-west-2 had a noisy spot reclaim wave earlier.
infra-oncall: autoscaler log snippet: "ScaleUp: requesting 8 g4dn.xlarge, error: LaunchFailures: capacity-constraints; retrying"
leo: we have two related problems: 1) spot churn left insufficient spare on-demand capacity in the configured nodepools, 2) subnet ENI quota hit on the target subnets.
maria: immediate mitigation idea: 1) enable fallback to a secondary nodepool (on-demand pool) in us-west-2 with different subnets, 2) scale that pool to 6, 3) cordon the misbehaving launch-template pool so CA stops requesting. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
aj: +1. Also disable the offending cronjobs that keep queuing pods (we saw a cronjob blast that created 120 jobs in 2m).
sanjay: doing cronjob disable now: `kubectl patch cronjob heavy-infer -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`
ops-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2026-03-18-usw2-provisioning-queue. Assigned to infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: Started emergency on-demand nodepool: nodepool-emer-ond-usw2, instance g5.xlarge, replicas=6. Kicking off attach to alternative subnets.
leo: also raised AWS support ticket for ENI throttling and requested temporary quota bump.
maria: rolling routing: set inference service fallback to nodepool-emer-ond-usw2 via route override, so new requests land on healthy nodes.
aj: pods are beginning to schedule to emergent pool, 18/24 Pending -> Running. Latency on requests dropped from 900ms tail to 220ms.
sanjay: still seeing a handful of preemptions for spot variants; reduced spot percentage on autoscaler groups to 20% to stabilize.
leo: cost note: emergency on-demand pool will add ~$4k/day if kept at current size; we should document decision and target to scale down asap.
maria: agreed — plan: 1) keep pool for 2 hours, 2) drain and scaledown to 0, 3) followup postmortem and runbook updates.
infra-oncall: followups: add subnet ENI monitoring alert, add autoscaler jitter/backoff tweak, add cronjob concurrency limits. I'll file the runbook PR.
aj: re-enabled heavy-infer cronjob with concurrencyPolicy: Forbid and suspend threshold 5 -> will rollout config after pool stable.
ops-bot: autoscaler: scale events suppressed for nodegroup-launch-template-spot due to repeated failures — switched to backoff.
maria: incident wrap: holding for 30m observation, if stable we'll close. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
